title: Amazon PPC Specialist
description:
About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Amazon PPC Specialist to manage and optimize advertising campaigns across multiple Amazon accounts.



This is a client-facing role, so the ideal candidate should be comfortable presenting performance updates, explaining strategy, answering client questions, and communicating recommendations clearly.



You will be responsible for day-to-day campaign management, performance analysis, keyword and targeting expansion, and identifying opportunities to improve sales and advertising efficiency. You will work closely with the Amazon Advertising Lead to execute account strategies and ensure campaigns are consistently optimized toward client goals.



Key Responsibilities

* Manage and optimize Amazon PPC campaigns across Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Brands Video, and Sponsored Display.

* Perform regular campaign audits and identify opportunities for optimization and expansion.

* Conduct keyword, search term, competitor, and ASIN targeting research.

* Build and manage brand, non-brand, product targeting, category targeting, and defensive campaigns.

* Monitor and optimize bids, budgets, placements, keywords, and product targets.

* Analyze performance across campaign, keyword, search term, and ASIN levels.

* Track key metrics including Spend, Sales, ACOS, ROAS, TACOS, CTR, CPC, CVR, and Orders.

* Identify high-performing search terms and opportunities for campaign expansion.

* Identify inefficient campaigns and targets and take appropriate optimization actions.

* Monitor budget utilization and ensure spend is aligned with account goals.

* Identify PPC opportunities that can support organic ranking and overall sales growth.

* Consider inventory, pricing, conversion rate, and other factors when analyzing advertising performance.

* Prepare and support weekly and monthly performance reporting.

* Join client calls and present campaign performance, insights, and next steps.

* Explain advertising strategy and performance in a clear and concise way.

* Respond to client questions and provide data-backed recommendations.

* Use AI tools and PPC management software to support analysis, reporting, campaign, optimization, research, and workflow efficiency.

* Clearly document optimizations, findings, tests, and recommended next steps.

* Stay current with Amazon Ads updates and advertising best practices.



Requirements

* At least 5+ years of hands-on Amazon PPC experience.

* Strong experience managing Amazon advertising accounts.

* Strong understanding of Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Brands Video, and Sponsored Display.

* Strong understanding of keyword targeting, product targeting, match types, search term harvesting, negatives, placements, bids, and budget management.

* Comfortable analyzing advertising data using Excel or Google Sheets.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

* Ability to diagnose changes in sales and advertising performance and determine potential causes.

* Ability to manage multiple accounts and priorities independently.

* Strong attention to detail.

* Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

* Comfortable speaking directly with clients and presenting performance updates and recommendations.

* Ability to communicate complex advertising topics in a simple, business-focused way.

* Comfortable using AI tools, automation, and PPC management software as part of day-to-day campaign management.

* Willingness to learn and adapt to new tools, platforms, and workflows.



Preferred Experience

* Strong Amazon PPC experience

* Amazon DSP experience is a plus



Performance KPIs

Performance will be evaluated across account results, execution quality, client management, and strategic contribution.

1. Account Performance

* Maintain PPC performance within the agreed client targets for ACoS, ROAS, TACoS, sales growth or profitability.

* Identify declining performance early and take corrective action.

* Improve efficiency or scale spend where opportunities exist.

* Maintain appropriate budget pacing throughout the month.

* Reduce unnecessary spend and continuously identify opportunities to improve campaign performance.



Target: Managed accounts meeting or progressing toward their agreed advertising objectives each month.



2. Optimization & Execution

* Complete scheduled account optimizations consistently and on time.

* Maintain clean campaign structures and accurate naming conventions.

* Regularly review search terms, keywords, ASIN targets, bids, placements, negatives, and budgets.

* Launch approved campaigns and tests within agreed timelines.

* Ensure campaign changes are properly documented.



Target: Planned optimizations and campaign tasks completed by deadline, with minimal execution errors.



3. Proactive Growth & Testing

* Identify new keyword, product targeting, category targeting, and campaign opportunities.

* Recommend and execute structured tests based on account performance.

* Surface opportunities to scale successful campaigns or products.

* Use PPC data to support broader recommendations around conversion, ranking, inventory, pricing, or listing performance.



Target: At least 2 meaningful growth or optimization recommendations per account per month, where applicable.



4. Client Communication

* Come prepared to client meetings with clear performance insights and recommended next steps.

* Communicate account changes and issues proactively.

* Respond to client questions accurately and professionally.

* Explain advertising performance in a way that is easy for clients to understand.



Target: Client deliverables completed on time, with no recurring communication or preparedness issues.



5. Reporting & Analysis

* Deliver accurate weekly and monthly reporting.

* Go beyond reporting metrics by explaining what changed, why it changed, and what should happen next.

* Ensure reporting data is accurate and aligned with Amazon Ads and account performance.



Target: 100% of reports delivered by deadline with accurate data



6. AI & Tool Adoption

* Effectively use approved AI tools, automation, and PPC management software to improve efficiency.

* Look for opportunities to automate repetitive work without compromising accuracy.

* Adopt new tools and workflows introduced by the team.



Target: Consistent use of approved tools and demonstrated improvement in workflow efficiency.



What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who can think beyond simply adjusting bids.



You should be able to look at an account and determine:

* Where there are opportunities to grow sales.

* Which keywords or targets should be expanded.

* Where advertising budget is being wasted.

* Which products should receive more advertising support.

* Why sales, conversion, or advertising performance changed.

* Whether performance issues are related to PPC, inventory, pricing, conversion, or other factors.

* What actions should be taken next.

* Where AI, automation, or PPC management tools can help improve efficiency and decision-making.



You should be comfortable managing campaigns independently, making data-backed recommendations, and confidently discussing those recommendations directly with clients.



Success in This Role

Success means consistently delivering against client advertising objectives, maintaining strong execution standards, proactively identifying growth opportunities, communicating clearly with clients, and managing accounts with minimal supervision.

title: YouTube Scriptwriter — Mysteries & Unexplained Events
description:
I’m looking for a strong, independent writer to create engaging YouTube scripts about strange sightings, unexplained events, and unusual encounters.



For examples of the writing quality I’m looking for—simple language, conversational delivery, and storytelling that’s extremely easy to follow—see:



• Carolina Case Files: 

• Lighthouse Mysteries: 

• MrBallen: 



PAY & DETAILS



• $100 USD per script, including research.

• 3,000–3,600 words per script.

• Freelance position with potential for ongoing work.

• Topics and writing guidelines will be provided.



INDEPENDENT WORK



You must be able to handle the entire script yourself: research, fact-checking, structure, writing, and proofreading.



Scripts must be complete and ready to narrate when submitted. I should not need to rewrite sentences, simplify the language, correct factual errors, or restructure the story.



The purpose of this position is to take scriptwriting off my plate. If I have to revise your work, this arrangement does not make sense for me. You need to understand the guidelines and consistently deliver finished scripts independently.



TOPICS



Strange sightings, unexplained events, and unusual encounters. No true crime. Choose stories with safe outcomes for everyone involved.



THE WRITING



Scripts must be extremely easy to follow, engaging, and natural when read aloud. Think of someone telling you a fascinating story in everyday language.



Absolutely no flowery language. None. No poetic descriptions, elaborate metaphors, or sentences dressed up to sound impressive.



For example:



• Don’t write: “An eerie silence draped itself over the sleepy town.”

  Write: “The town was quiet.”



• Don’t write: “The moon cast its silver veil across the lonely stretch of asphalt.”

  Write: “The moon lit the road.”



• Don’t write: “An icy wave of terror gripped him as he gazed upon the mysterious figure.”

  Write: “He was frightened when he saw the figure.”



The writing must not sound AI-generated at all. No robotic phrasing, generic suspense lines, awkward transitions, or repeated points.



I’m looking for a strong opening, a clear sequence of events, and interesting details that keep people listening. Let the events make the story interesting.



Research each topic carefully, provide source links, and distinguish documented facts from witness accounts or speculation. Do not invent details or dialogue. Include pronunciation guides in parentheses for unfamiliar names and places.



TO APPLY



Use Ghost as the subject line of your application and include:



1. Why you would be a good fit, including any relevant writing experience.

2. At least one existing writing sample. Multiple samples are preferred.

3. Links to published videos using your writing, if available, and your role in creating them.

4. Your usual turnaround time for a 3,000–3,600-word script.



I’m hoping to find a reliable writer for a long-term working relationship.

title: Customer support
description:
Read this entire post before applying. If you skim it, you will fail the application in the first five seconds and we will both have wasted our time. That is not a threat — it's a favor. This job is not for most people, and I'd rather you find that out now.





WHAT THIS JOB ACTUALLY IS

We are a Swedish e-commerce company running several brands. Every brand gets customer
s every day, and every one of them needs a correct answer the same day. Forever.



Your job: clear the support inboxes every day. Different brands, different languages, the same questions over and over:



"Where is my delivery?"

Order not received.

Product not as expected.

Returns and exchanges.

General questions about the brand.



The
s are boring. The job is not. Here is what a normal day actually looks like:



Open the inboxes. Look each order up in Shopify. Find the tracking. Reply in the customer's language using DeepL, following our reply guide.

When tracking has been dead for a week, you do not tell the customer "please wait." You message our shipping agents in China, get an answer, and then tell the customer what is actually happening and when.

When a customer opens a dispute with their bank, you collect the evidence — order, tracking, delivery proof, your
 thread — and submit it to the payment provider. Before the deadline. Without being reminded.

When the same problem shows up three times in one week, you write it down and tell us. Once, with numbers.



The tools: Shopify admin,
, DeepL, the carriers' tracking pages, the payment provider's dispute portal, and a chat with our China agents. We teach you our setup in week one. Shopify admin you must already know: previous hands-on experience in Shopify admin is required.





THE ONE THING THIS JOB IS REALLY ABOUT

We are in Sweden and we spend our days running ads. We are not going to sit next to you. If you message us "what should I do?" three times a day, this job has failed — for both of us.



The rule is simple. Before anything reaches us, you have already tried to solve it. When it still has to reach us, it arrives like this — four lines, nothing else:



The problem: Order 4471, tracking dead for 11 days, customer threatening a chargeback.

What I already did: Checked the carrier page, asked the China agent on Monday and again on Wednesday, no reply.

What I propose: Offer a replacement now, refund only if there is no scan by Friday.

What I need from you: A yes or a no.



That is the whole job in four lines. Anyone can answer "where is my order" when the tracking works. I am hiring the person who knows what to do when it doesn't — and who d
 first and asks second.



Quick question, and I mean it: a customer writes in Danish, and DeepL is down for the whole day. What do you do? Make your answer the very last thing you say in your application video. You'll see why below.





WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT, IN THIS EXACT ORDER

1. You show up. Every single day, Saturday and Sunday included. Not "most days." Not "I had internet problems." Every day.

2. The inbox is cleared inside your window, every day. Nothing sits for more than 24 hours without a reply.

3. You d
 first and ask second. Every time something reaches us, it comes with your proposed solution.

4. You stay. We are building a team, not renting an assistant for two months.

5. Your English and your tone are good enough — and get better.



Notice that skill is fifth on this list. That is not a mistake. The one skill you must bring is Shopify admin. Everything else we can teach you: our brands, our reply guide, our shipping, our tone — we have a whole system for it, and the person who reads this carefully and types "kanelbulle" as the first word of the subject line when applying is already showing me the exact trait I'm hiring for. It is not mentioned in the subject line structure below, but it is supposed to be the first word, then the structure. What we cannot teach is a person who opens the inbox every single day for the next two years, weekends included, and who would rather make a decision than wait for one.





HOURS — READ THIS PART HONESTLY

This is work on demand. There is no fixed shift. The rule is simple: the inbox is cleared every day, 7 days a week, inside 10:00–17:00 Swedish time. If you are in the Philippines, that window is 17:00–00:00 right now (16:00–23:00 in summer). You d
 when inside it. The workload has grown fast: right now the job takes several hours every day, and it keeps growing as we add brands and tasks. Weekends are never optional.



You log the hours you actually work, and you are paid for them. More hours come with more brands and more tasks.



If you cannot open the inbox every single day, including weekends, do not apply. That is the entire job.





PAY — READ THIS PART SLOWLY

Hourly rate, paid twice a month, on time, every time. We have never missed a payment and we never will.



The rate ladder, in writing:



Start: $2.50 USD per hour.

After 1 month: $3.00 USD per hour.

After 3 months: $3.50 USD per hour.

After 6 months: $4.00 USD per hour.



Every step is automatic if you are still clearing the inbox every day. It goes into your agreement on day one. You will never have to ask me for a raise, and I will never "forget." The first raise comes after ONE month. Not six. Not "we'll see." One month.



On top of that:



$20 USD consistency bonus every month you open the inbox on every single day with zero missed days. This is the easiest money in the job, and it is entirely within your control.

$3 USD per Trustpilot review. Every 4- or 5-star review from a real customer that mentions you by name. Uncapped, and this is the real upside. A customer who was angry on Monday and names you in a 5-star review on Thursday is exactly the job, and you get paid for it every time it happens. Each review is matched to a real order before it is paid.



One line on that, because it matters: you never ask a customer for a rating, you never offer a customer anything for a review, and you never write one yourself. One fake, bought or nudged review and the seat is gone the same day. The reviews you get paid for are the ones you earned by fixing the problem so well that the customer wanted to say your name.



You are paid for the hours you actually work, not for counting
s. Some days are calmer. Some days are a full inbox and a dispute deadline. Either way, the day is cleared.





WHAT COUNTS AS DONE

Every customer
 that arrived before 17:00 Swedish time is answered the same day, in the customer's language, following the reply guide, with the order looked up in Shopify. Every dispute is answered before its deadline. Anything that reaches us comes in the four-line format above. Not a taste judgment. If I send something back, I tell you exactly why in one sentence, and it counts once you fix it.





WHO SHOULD NOT APPLY

Please save us both the time. Do not apply if:



You cannot open the inbox every single day, Saturday and Sunday included.

Your internet is unreliable and you have no backup connection.

You have no plan for brownouts or power cuts.

You need someone to tell you what to do for each
.

You take angry customers personally, or argue with them.

You have never worked in Shopify admin for a real store. Not "seen it" — worked in it.

You are not comfortable recording a short video of yourself with your camera on.

You want to negotiate the rate upward before you've proven a single month.

You are looking for a placeholder while you search for something better.

You want the "future tasks" at the bottom of this post to be the job now. They come after months of a cleared inbox, not before.



I'm not being harsh for fun. I'd rather describe the job exactly than lose a good person who wanted a different one.





HOW TO APPLY — THIS IS THE FIRST TEST

Ninety percent of applicants will get this wrong. That's the point.



1. Subject line, formatted EXACTLY like this:

| [most customer
s you have ever answered in ONE day] | [years using Shopify admin] | [hours/day you can work] | [days/week you can work] | [your download speed from speedtest.net]



Example: XXXXXX | 45 | 2 | 2 | 7 | 40mbps



Wrong format or a missing field — deleted unread. If the Shopify field says 0, deleted unread. No exceptions, no second chances.



2. Your message contains ONE thing: a link to a Loom video. Nothing else. No written answers, no cover letter, no CV.



It must be Loom (
). Not YouTube, not Google Drive, not a file. The free Loom plan is enough. Set the link so anyone with it can watch. Maximum 5 minutes. In English. Camera on, your face visible the whole time.



In the video, cover these six things, in this order:



1. Who you are, and the most customer
s you have ever answered in one day. For which store, and what kind of tickets.

2. Your Shopify experience. Which stores, for how long, and what you actually did in Shopify admin. Then: the first thing you open in Shopify admin when a customer says the package hasn't arrived, and what you look at there.

3. Your setup. Computer, internet provider, backup internet, and what you do when the power goes out. Open speedtest.net on your screen and run it while you record. The number must match your subject line.

4. Longevity. The longest you have ever stayed in one role or with one client, how long, and why it ended. A short history with an honest reason beats an inflated one.

5. What would make you quit this job. Everyone has a breaking point. Tell me yours. I trust the person who names it far more than the person who says "nothing."

6. The last thing you say in the video: the answer to the question I asked you earlier in this post. If it isn't there, you didn't read the post. If it is, I already know two things about you.



Never show a client's Shopify admin, customer names or orders on your screen. Protecting customer data is part of this job, so it is part of the test.



3. If I message you, reply within 24 hours. If you don't, I move on to the next applicant. Answering fast is part of the job, so it is part of the test.





THE THREE STAGES

Stage 1 — The application above. A Loom of up to 5 minutes. Most people won't do it.



Stage 2 — The inbox test. Unpaid. If your video is sharp, I send you five real customer
s (names removed) in three languages, our reply guide, and access to DeepL. You return five written replies within 24 hours. One of the five has no answer in the guide. I am watching what you do with that one: guess, ask a smart question, or find it. Anything that has to reach me comes in the four-line format. I am not grading style. I am grading: did you follow the guide exactly, did you deliver on time, and did you d
 before you asked. This is a real preview of the daily job.



Stage 3 — Paid trial week on one brand's live inbox. Real customers, real China agents, real feedback. This is where the seat is won.





WHAT YOU GET IF YOU WIN IT

One company, several brands, the same people every day. You choose when you work inside the window. Pay on time, twice a month, without ever having to ask. A rate that grows on a schedule you can see, and hours that grow with the work. Someone who tells you exactly what's wrong in one sentence so you can fix it and get better fast.



And a real path. Once the inbox has been cleared every day for months, the next tasks are real: finding products, searching for ad videos, writing ad copy, product descriptions, talking to UGC creators and influencers. We train you for them. But that comes after, not instead.



And the upside has no ceiling: every customer who names you in a 4- or 5-star review is $3 in your pocket, forever, on top of everything above.



If you're the kind of person who is tired of clients who never answer, and who just wants a seat, a standard to hit, and to be paid reliably for hitting it — this is that.



Show me you can follow instructions, and show me you can d
. That's the whole first test.

title: YouTube Script Writer and Researcher - 10-15 Minute Breakdowns of Viral Public Incidents
description:
We're hiring a writer who is also a strong researcher to script long-form YouTube videos about viral public i
. These are the "Karen" confrontations you see on TikTok and Instagram: road rage, parking lots, flights, restaurants and stores. Each video tells one story from start to finish: what happened on camera, who the person turned out to be, how they explained themselves, and what it cost them, from losing a job to criminal charges. Videos run 8–15 minutes. We're looking for someone to work with us on an ongoing basis.



The research matters as much as the writing. Every fact in a script must come from a source you can link, and anything that is only one person's claim has to be presented as a claim.



WHAT YOU'LL DO



- Find stories. Each week, pitch 3–5 viral i
 where the person has been publicly identified and has faced consequences, with links. Sources include TikTok, Instagram, X, Reddit, local news and commentary channels.



- Research each approved story into a timeline: the original clip and who posted it, how the person was identified, their apology or excuse, employer statements, police reports, court records and charges, and any updates since.



- Check everything. Confirm identities through news reports or the person's own response, never a guess from the comments. Tell proven facts apart from claims, and say what is still unknown.



- Write the script to be read aloud, in the order below. Mark every point where a clip plays, with the clip's link and timestamps.



- Include a source list with every script: a link for each fact.



- Track stories you've written about and flag new developments for follow-up videos, such as court dates, lawsuits and new statements.



HOW EACH SCRIPT IS BUILT



1. Cold open: the most shocking few seconds of the clip.

2. Hook: one or two sentences that sum up the i
 and tease the consequences.

3. Context: the exact date, time, place and business, who filmed it and what happened before the recording started.

4. The clip, then a short explanation of what we just watched.

5. Who they are: name, age and job as reported, and who identified them.

6. Their side: the apology, statement or excuse, checked against the evidence.

7. The consequences: firing, charges, bail and court dates, business reviews.

8. Closing line: a sharp callback to something earlier in the story.



EXAMPLE OPENING (an imaginary story, to show the style)



[CLIP 0:04–0:09: "It's two dollars! Two!"]

So, you're working the Saturday shift at a self-serve car wash, and a man in a brand-new pickup d
 the token machine has robbed him. Of two dollars. By the end of the afternoon he's hit a 17-year-old attendant with a pressure washer, and by Monday his own company has put out a statement about him. It's March 8th, at a car wash in Mesa, Arizona. The attendant, Jordan, is restocking towels when the man waves him over. Take a look.

[CLIP 0:00–0:52]

According to the police report, the attendant asked him to step back from the machine twice before the hose came up.



The tone is conversational and dry, never shouty, and always on the side of the person being harassed. The humour comes from specific details, not insults.



WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



- Excellent written English that sounds natural to an American audience when read aloud.



- Real research skills. You can find and read news reports, court record searches, police statements and company announcements, and you know a primary source from a repost.



- Accuracy and care. You attribute claims ("she says", "according to police"), call charges charges and not convictions, and never state a guess as fact.



- Storytelling. You can turn a messy timeline into a script that keeps people watching to the end.



- A dry sense of humour that comes from details, not name-calling.



- Comfort with heated footage, including swearing and racial slurs. Scripts describe slurs and never repeat them.



- Good judgement about privacy. Scripts never include home addresses, phone numbers or details about family members or children.



- Reliable deadlines.



- Bonus: experience writing or researching for YouTube commentary, true crime or news channels, or you already watch channels like That Danesh Guy.



Workload: To start, 2 scripts a week, each about 1,200–2,000 words, plus weekly story pitches.



Turnaround: Each script is due within 3 days of its story being approved.



HOW TO APPLY



Start your application with the word "papaya" and include:



1. Your
 address



2. Links to 1–3 scripts or long-form pieces you've written (Google Docs set so anyone with the link can view)



3. Links to any YouTube channels or videos you've written or researched for, what you did and when (or "none yet")



4. A short research sample: pick a viral public i
 from the last 6 months where the person was identified and faced consequences, and give its timeline in 5–8 bullet points with a source link for each point



5. A sample opening for that same i
 (60–100 words), written to be read aloud



6. Your expected rate (per script of about 1,500 words, or per month)



7. How many scripts a week you can take on, and your usual working hours (Philippine time)



8. Your 
 username



Applications that skip the code word or any of items 1–7 won't be reviewed.

title: SEO Specialist
description:
SEO Specialist



Full-Time | Remote | Minimum 2 Years' Experience



About the Role



We're looking for an experienced, proactive and detail-oriented SEO Specialist to join our growing digital marketing team.



This isn't an entry-level position. We're looking for someone with at least 2 years of hands-on SEO experience, preferably within a digital marketing agency, who understands what it takes to improve organic search performance and deliver measurable results for clients.



You'll be responsible for implementing and supporting SEO strategies across a portfolio of client websites, working across technical SEO, on-page optimisation, content strategy, blogging and emerging areas of search, including Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) and Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO).



We're particularly interested in someone who understands how SEO is evolving, enjoys problem-solving, and is comfortable using technology and automation to improve efficiency and campaign outcomes.



If you're someone who takes pride in your work, communicates well and doesn't need to be micromanaged, we'd love to hear from you.



Key Responsibilities



1. Technical SEO



- Conduct technical SEO audits and identify website issues affecting organic search performance.

- Identify and troubleshoot indexing, crawling, website structure and technical optimisation issues.

- Understand HTML and basic website code, including the ability to identify and resolve straightforward HTML issues.

- Implement and optimise schema markup and structured data.

- Monitor Google Search Console and identify opportunities or potential issues.

- Work with developers to communicate and resolve technical SEO requirements.



2. On-Page SEO



- Conduct keyword research and identify commercially relevant search opportunities.

- Optimise website pages, metadata, headings, internal linking and URL structures.

- Develop keyword mapping and content optimisation strategies.

- Analyse search intent and ensure content aligns with user expectations.

- Identify opportunities to improve existing website content and organic rankings.



3. Content & Blogging



- Develop content strategies aligned with SEO objectives.

- Research, brief and optimise SEO blog articles.

- Identify topical authority and content cluster opportunities.

- Ensure content is well-structured, engaging and optimised for search.

- Review and edit content to maintain high editorial and grammatical standards.



IMPORTANT – Application Instructions



Before applying, make sure you include "Cool jellybeans" at the very top of your application. It's a little way for me to make sure you've taken the time to read the full job description!



4. GEO & AEO (AI Search)



- Understand Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) and Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO).

- Identify opportunities to improve brand visibility across AI-powered search platforms, including ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and other emerging platforms.

- Understand how structured content, topical authority, entity optimisation and credible sources influence AI search visibility.

- Keep up to date with developments in AI search and the changing search landscape.



5. Automation & Technology



- Identify opportunities to automate repetitive SEO tasks and improve workflow efficiency.

- Have a working understanding of automation platforms and tools such as Make, Zapier or n8n.

- Understand how AI tools and automation can be incorporated into SEO workflows.

- Be comfortable working with HTML and understanding how websites function.

- Demonstrate an interest in emerging SEO tools, technologies and processes.



6. Reporting & Communication



- Monitor keyword rankings, organic traffic and other key SEO performance metrics.

- Interpret SEO data and identify actionable opportunities.

- Prepare clear, accurate and meaningful client reports.

- Communicate campaign progress, challenges and recommendations to the wider team.

- Collaborate with other team members to deliver client outcomes.



Skills & Experience



Essential Requirements



- Minimum 2 years of practical SEO experience.

- Previous experience working within a digital marketing agency is highly regarded.

- Strong understanding of technical SEO and on-page optimisation.

- Good knowledge of keyword research, search intent and content strategy.

- Experience with SEO content writing, optimisation and blogging.

- Working knowledge of HTML and basic website code.

- Understanding of SEO automation and workflow efficiencies.

- Familiarity with Google Search Console and Google Analytics 4.

- Strong written and spoken English.

- Excellent attention to detail.

- Strong communication and problem-solving skills.

- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.



Highly Regarded



- Experience with GEO and AEO.

- Experience with WordPress and other CMS platforms.

- Knowledge of schema markup and structured data.

- Experience with Make, Zapier, n8n or similar automation platforms.

- Familiarity with tools such as Ahrefs, SEMrush, Screaming Frog, Ubersuggest or similar.

- Understanding of Google algorithm updates and emerging SEO trends.

- Experience managing multiple SEO campaigns simultaneously.



The Person We're Looking For



Technical skills are important, but attitude and approach matter just as much.



We're looking for someone who is:



- A problem solver: You don't just identify problems; you look for solutions and take initiative.

- A strong communicator: You can explain technical concepts clearly and communicate effectively with colleagues and clients.

- Detail-oriented: You take pride in producing accurate, high-quality work.

- Proactive: You stay informed about SEO developments and actively look for ways to improve.

- A team player: You collaborate, share knowledge and contribute positively to the team.

- Curious: You're interested in technology, automation and how AI is changing the search landscape.

- Accountable: You take ownership of your work and follow tasks through to completion.



What We Offer



- Fully remote working environment.

- Opportunity to work across a diverse range of industries and SEO campaigns.

- Exposure to traditional SEO and emerging AI search strategies.

- A collaborative team environment.

- Opportunities for professional development and growth.

- The opportunity to contribute ideas and improve internal processes.



How to Apply



We want to hear from people who are genuinely interested in the role and confident in their SEO abilities.



As part of your application, you MUST submit a short introductory video (2–3 minutes).



In your video, please cover the following:



1. Introduction: Tell us a little about yourself and briefly explain your SEO experience.

2. Practical Experience: Tell us about an SEO campaign or project you've personally worked on. What was the challenge, what did you do, and what were the results?

3. SEO Knowledge: Explain your understanding of technical SEO, GEO/AEO and how you think AI is changing the search landscape.

4. Automation: Tell us about an automation tool or process you've used, or something you would like to automate within an SEO workflow.

5. Why You? Why do you believe you'd be a good fit for this position?



We're not looking for a perfectly scripted presentation. We want to get a feel for your communication skills, personality, knowledge and genuine enthusiasm for SEO.



Important: Applications without an introductory video will not be considered.



We look forward to hearing from you!

title: Clip Editor – Stream Clips to Vertical Shorts for TikTok, Reels & YouTube Shorts (50-100+ clips/week, ongoing, remote)
description:
I send you clips from a streamer’s channel, and you turn them into polished vertical shorts for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and other platforms. The clips are already picked. Your job is to trim, frame, caption, and export. This is ongoing weekly work for the right person.



THE JOB



You’ll get a sheet of clip links from the streamer’s clips page, with IN/OUT points within each clip and the line being clipped

50+ clips per week, delivered in batches of 10–15

One export per clip works across TikTok, Reels, and Shorts

Expected pace: about 10 clips per hour once you’re set up. If a clip takes you 20 minutes, this isn’t the right fit.



OUTPUT SPECS



9:16 vertical, exported at 1080×1920

Always crop to fill, never letterbox. Scaling the crop up to 1080×1920 is expected.

Layout: [facecam only / facecam stacked over gameplay]. A reference clip is provided.

Length: 15–50 seconds

Captions: burned in, 2–4 words per line, high contrast, [font / color / position]. A template is provided.

Keep captions and faces inside platform safe zones, clear of the TikTok/Reels buttons and caption area

Audio normalized to [-14 LUFS]

Export: MP4, H.264, [30/60] fps



QUALITY BAR



Cuts land within 0.5s of the IN/OUT points. Use that window to start and end on a clean word. Mid-word openings are the most common rejection.

The hook is visible in the first 1.5 seconds. If the clip doesn’t allow that, flag it in your batch notes instead of guessing.

Framing is head-and-chest, centered in the upper part of the frame, never cropped at the eyes. Any exceptions will be noted in the sheet.

Captions match the audio exactly. Fix auto-caption errors on names, slang, game terms, and crosstalk. A glossary of names and terms is provided.

Flag any clip that’s missing its setup, has muted audio, or is too low quality to use.



WHAT TO CUT AROUND



Ads, sponsor reads, or brand promo segments

BRB screens, countdowns, intro stings, or raid shoutouts

Dead air. Five seconds of silence in a clip means it’s wrong.



If any of these fall inside a clip, remove them with a clean jump cut, or flag the clip if removing them breaks it.



PAY AND TERMS



Paid test batch: 10 clips (about 1 hour) at $3.35/hour

Ongoing: $3.25–4.50/hour, about 10-15 hours per week for 50-100+ clips (roughly $150–250/month)

Hours tracked per batch [time tracker / reported hours]

Paid every Friday via PayPal, crypto or others.

One revision round per clip.

24-hour turnaround per batch



REQUIREMENTS



Video editing experience, with a portfolio of short-form vertical work (TikTok, Reels, or Shorts)

A computer that can smoothly edit and export 1080p footage

Editing software that supports reframing, burned-in captions, and audio normalization (Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, CapCut desktop, or similar)

A reliable internet connection for downloading clips and uploading batches on time

Familiarity with platform safe zones and short-form caption styles

Clear, responsive communication

title: Software User Tester (US Real Estate App) - Full-Time, 40 hrs/week, $3.50/hr
description:
THE JOB IN ONE SENTENCE



Use Lot Decoder all day, in every US state, the way real agents, investors and builders do, and find every wrong answer, broken screen and confusing word before our users do.



- Hours: full time, 40 hours a week, Monday to Friday

- Pay: $3.50/hr, as an independent contractor

- Where: remote, Philippines-based

- Team: you find the problems. A Zoning Reviewer fixes zoning numbers and a Price Accuracy Checker fixes prices. Everything else goes to the owner.



WHAT IS LOT DECODER?



Agents, investors and builders type in an address. Lot Decoder tells them what they can build on that lot and what it might cost and earn, in any US city. Deal Finder searches a whole city for empty lots that could make money. If any of that is wrong, someone could lose real money on a bad deal. Your job is to find it first.



WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU



This is a high-output role. These are the numbers you'll be measured on every week.



- Deal Finder searches: Weeks 1–2: 60 a week; Weeks 3–4: 80 a week; Week 5 on: 100 a week

- Full reports opened and checked: Weeks 1–2: 20 a week; Weeks 3–4: 35 a week; Week 5 on: 50 a week

- Different US states covered: Weeks 1–2: 3 a week; Weeks 3–4: 4 a week; Week 5 on: 5 a week (all 50 states in about 10 weeks)

- Confirmed defects filed: Weeks 1–2: 15 a week; Weeks 3–4: 25 a week; Week 5 on: 30 a week

- Defects the owner can repeat from your steps: 90%

- Fixed defects re-tested: within 1 business day

- Stop-ship defects reported: within 1 hour



What counts as a confirmed defect: a real problem that someone else can see by following your steps. Duplicates, guesses and "I think this might be wrong" without proof don't count. One real wrong-money defect is worth more than ten typos.



As the app gets better, defects get harder to find. The defect target will be reset with you every month so it stays tough but fair.



Missing the weekly targets two weeks in a row means we talk about whether the role is a fit.



YOUR DAILY ROUTINE



Step 1: Start of day (15 minutes)



1. Open the Team page (
/#/team), pick "Test plan" and tap Clock in. Your hours count automatically from here.

2. Open the Defects card. Re-test every report marked Fixed (see "How to re-test a fix" below).

3. Read "Test plan for today" on the Team page: today's new city, the repeat city and the focus. Tap Next to open Deal Finder already set to that city.



Step 2: Run Deal Finder searches (about 3 hours)



Run 20 searches a day: 1 or 2 in today's new city, and the rest as repeats in cities already searched (try a different ZIP code, lot size or development type). Repeats cost us much less and still test the app. If you see "today's budget reached", move on to Step 4. For each search:



1. Open Deal Finder in Lot Decoder and type the place from your test plan.

2. Time it. Write down how long until the first lots show, and how long until the search finishes.

3. Check the top 5 cards and 2 random cards from lower down. For each card, check:

   - Is it a real, empty lot? Open the map or aerial photo. A house, building or parking lot on it is a defect.

   - Is it in the place you searched? A lot from another city or ZIP code is a defect.

   - Is it really for sale (for-sale cards)? Open the listing link. Sold, pending or a dead link is a defect.

   - Is it government land? Owner names like "City of...", "County of...", "State of..." or "Housing Authority" are defects.

   - Does the zoning label make sense? Compare the card's zone with the county's official zoning map. A different zone is a Zoning defect.

   - Do the owner and mailing details make sense (off-market cards)?

   - Does every link and button work?

   - Can a first-time user understand every word? Anything confusing is a Wording defect.



Step 3: Open full reports (about 3 hours)



Open 10 reports a day, all from lots in that day's Deal Finder results: 5 by clicking the card, and 5 by typing that lot's address into the home page.



For each report:



1. Check the lot: is the outline on the map the right lot? Is the address right?

2. Check the zoning numbers (lot size, height, setbacks) against the county zoning map and the city code. File any that look wrong as Zoning defects with the code link.

3. Check the sales the report used: are they real sales nearby, of the same property type the report plans to build (house, townhome, condo, apartments, retail or industrial)? Any that are far away or a different type go in as Price defects. If the finished sale price looks far above or below similar sold properties nearby, file it as a Price defect too. Don't do the full price check yourself; the Price Checker does that.

4. Read every sentence. Anything that contradicts another part of the report, or that a beginner wouldn't understand, is a defect.

5. Try every button: save, share, presentations, offer letter and contact owner. Don't send anything to a real owner, agent or customer.



Step 4: Try to break it (about 1 hour)



Every day, try 5 things a real user might do by mistake:



- type an address with a typo, no city, or a unit number

- search a tiny town, a rural county, or a place with no empty lots

- use your phone in portrait and landscape

- go back, refresh or switch tabs in the middle of a search

- run two searches at once in two tabs



Step 5: File every defect the same day



Every defect gets one report: tap "Something look wrong? Report a problem" at the bottom of the page, on the page where you found it. See "How to file a defect" below. File Stop-ship defects within 1 hour, and also message Debbie in Skool right away.



Step 6: End of day (5 minutes)



1. On the Team page, tap Clock out. Your hours, searches, reports and defects are counted automatically and show in the Team feed.

2. Message Debbie in Skool with 2 lines: the worst thing you found today, and anything blocking you.



HOW TO FILE A DEFECT



One report per problem. Write these in the report box, one per line, and tap "Add a screenshot".



- Date: Today's date

- Type: Zoning, Price, Wrong lot, Not empty, Not for sale, Government land, Slow, Broken, Wording, Other

- Severity: Stop-ship: wrong money, wrong lot, a crash, or something a user could lose money on. Major: wrong information that a careful user might catch. Minor: wording, layout or a small glitch.

- Where: The full address or place searched, and the page link

- Steps: Numbered steps someone else can follow to see it

- Expected: What should have happened

- What happened: What actually happened, with the exact numbers or words

- Proof: A screenshot, plus a link to the official source (zoning map, code, sold listing)

- Device: Phone or computer, and the browser



Where it goes: Zoning defects go to the Zoning Reviewer, Price defects go to the Price Accuracy Checker, and everything else goes to the owner. The Type you write routes it. You don't need to message anyone except for Stop-ship defects.



Before filing: check the Defects card for the same address or problem. If it's already there, don't file it twice.



HOW TO RE-TEST A FIX



1. Follow the report's Steps exactly.

2. If the problem is gone, mark it Passed in the Defects card.

3. If it's still there, mark it Failed and file a new report with a new screenshot that mentions the first one.

4. Also check one other place with the same kind of problem (another city, another lot). If it shows up there, file a new report and mention the first one. Fixes must work everywhere, not just on one address.



RULES



1. Never contact a real owner, seller, agent or customer. Contact tools are tested only up to the final send button.

2. Use only the test account the owner gives you, and stay under the daily search limit. Searches cost real money.

3. Proof beats opinion. Every Zoning or Price defect needs an official link or a real sold listing.

4. Report what you see, not what you guess the cause is.

5. Keep everything confidential: the app, its numbers, and every defect report.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



- You've done software testing (QA), or you've worked in US real estate support and are relentlessly detail-minded.

- You know how to read a US county parcel map or a listing, or can learn it in your first week.

- You write steps so clearly that someone else can repeat them the first time.

- You stay sharp doing the same kind of check 100 times a week.

- A plus: experience with US zoning maps, US real estate, or testing mobile apps.



TRAINING IN YOUR FIRST 30 DAYS (PAID)



1. Finish all 8 Lot Decoder courses and their quizzes in our Skool community within your first 30 days.

2. Be active in the community: introduce yourself, then make at least 3 helpful posts or replies a week.

3. Course time is paid at your normal hourly rate once your access is on. On the Team page, pick "Training" when you clock in. Studying before your access is on is optional and unpaid.

4. In the community, label yourself as "Lot Decoder Team". Never pose as a customer.



HOW IT STARTS



1. Paid trial: 4 hours on the live app, paid at $3.50/hr. File as many confirmed defects as you can. We grade every one.

2. 90 days: we review your defect count, quality and weekly targets together.

3. Contract: independent contractor agreement with confidentiality and work-for-hire terms.



TO APPLY



Send:



1. A few lines about your testing or real estate experience.

2. Confirm that $3.50/hr for 40 hours a week works for you.

3. One defect you found in any website or app, written with Steps, Expected and What happened.

title: Operations Assistant
description:
Operations Assistant



Location: Remote – Philippines  

Hours: Full-time | 40 hours per week | 5pm–2am Philippines time (aligned with UK working hours)  

Salary: £500–£700 per month, depending on experience and skillset, plus performance bonus and paid UK bank holidays.



About Innermost:



At Innermost, we believe better health comes from finding the right balance between nature and science. Inspired by traditional ingredients and powered by modern, evidence-based research, we've developed a fresh approach to wellness. We combine natural ingredients with cutting-edge science to create products that are effective, transparent and rooted in quality. Our mission is simple: to make better health easy. Founded in London, Innermost has experienced significant growth since launch, and we have ambitious plans for the future. We're building a challenger brand with the ambition to change the way people think about health and wellness. If you'd like to be part of a growing international business and contribute to something ambitious, we'd love to hear from you. Learn more at 



The Role:



We're looking for a highly organised, proactive and detail-oriented Operations Assistant to join our growing team. This is a varied role covering multiple areas of the business, including finance, accounting, supply chain, inventory management, reporting and customer experience. You'll join our existing Operations team, working alongside four other team members who are based remotely in the Philippines and support the day-to-day running of our international business.



This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving problems and working across different areas of a business. You'll need to be comfortable managing multiple priorities, working independently and taking responsibility for ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time.



Key Responsibilities:



Operations >>



- Executing daily, weekly and monthly operational tasks to ensure the smooth running of the business.

- Supporting the coordination and management of internal processes and workflows.

- Identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and streamline processes.



Finance & Accounting >>



- Bookkeeping and maintaining accurate financial records.

- Bank and account reconciliations.

- Managing accounts payable and receivable.

- Supporting financial administration and reporting.



Inventory & Supply Chain >>



- Monitoring inventory levels across products and warehouses.

- Coordinating stock replenishment orders and monitoring deliveries.

- Maintaining accurate inventory records and identifying potential stock shortages.

- Supporting supplier and logistics coordination.



Customer Experience >>



- Managing customer enquiries and providing timely, professional responses.

- Resolving customer issues and escalating matters where necessary.

- Supporting customer retention and customer success initiatives.

- Ensuring customers receive a consistently positive experience.



Reporting & Data Management >>



- Assisting with weekly and monthly management reporting.

- Maintaining spreadsheets, databases and operational records.

- Analysing data and helping identify trends, discrepancies and opportunities for improvement.



Skills & Experience:



- A degree in Business, Management, Finance, Accounting or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

- Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

- Excellent numerical and analytical abilities.

- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Excel, including Pivot Tables, lookup functions, SUMIFS and working with larger datasets.

- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.

- Ability to work independently, take initiative and solve problems without constant supervision.

- A proactive approach to work, with a willingness to take ownership and responsibility.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambitious environment with high expectations.

- A positive attitude and willingness to support colleagues and contribute to a team.



Additional Information:



This is a full-time position requiring 40 working hours per week, spread across five days (eight working hours per day, plus a one-hour break). Salary of £500–£700 per month, depending on experience, qualifications and skillset. In addition, you will receive an end-of-year performance bonus and paid time off for eight UK bank holidays, despite not being required to work on those days. Innermost is based in London, United Kingdom, and our core working hours are 9am–6pm UK time. The corresponding Philippines working hours are generally 5pm–2am.



How to Apply:



We'd love to hear from candidates who believe they have the skills, experience and attitude to succeed in this role. Please submit your CV along with some additional information about your experience and skillset. We'd also like you to record a short 60-second video explaining why you believe you'd be a good fit for the position and what you could bring to the team.



Please also answer the following questions when applying:



1. Where do you currently live? Please specify whether you live in a city or a village.

2. What is your internet connection speed, and do you have reliable electricity in your area?

3. What IT equipment do you have available to support your work? For example, Macbook, laptop or desktop computer, additional monitor, headset and backup internet connection.



Please submit your application through the OnlineJobs.ph messaging platform and include a link to your video recording (Loom is preferred). Shortlisted candidates will be contacted regarding the next steps, which may include an interview over Zoom.



**Please follow the application instructions carefully. Applications that do not include the requested information and video may not be considered.**



Thank you, and we look forward to hearing from you.
